basis: Defined by neurodevelopmental impairment, dystonia and tremor; an enzyme's role in purine synthesis alone does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Primary meningeal tumor; recurrence does not establish involvement of another organ.
Benign myofibroblastic tumor of lymph-node stroma; neither a blood-cell neoplasm nor lymphoma. Nodal stroma falls outside the specified axes.
Inherited neurologic sleep disorder; diabetes and obstructive sleep apnea are separately diagnosed comorbidities, not direct organ damage from narcolepsy.
Developmental impairment and delayed skeletal maturation define the syndrome; myopia affects 30-79%, supporting ocular involvement.
Tick-borne infectious illness; its transient erythema migrans-like rash does not establish lasting skin damage.
HPV-associated papilloma occupies the laryngeal airway; local viral infection underlies the characteristic lesion.
Carcinoma in situ originates in bronchial epithelium.
Sensorineural deafness and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism define Perrault syndrome; seizures and microcephaly each occur in 3/10, meeting the neurologic threshold.
Thymic epithelial carcinoma; thymus is outside the specified axes. This is neither lymphoma nor an immune-mediated disease.
Inflammation surrounding bile ducts is hepatic; inflammation alone does not establish infection or an autoimmune mechanism.
Cerebellopontine-angle schwannomas usually arise from the vestibular nerve; auditory dysfunction from direct nerve involvement occurs in most patients (>70%).
Defining upper-limb, craniofacial skeletal and nasal malformations; cardiac defects, encephalocele, callosal agenesis and choanal atresia are occasional (<30%).
Benign adipose tumor arising within the rectum.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining developmental and structural CNS abnormalities; muscle enzyme deficiency alone does not establish myopathy.
Isolated spermatogenic failure and male infertility affect reproductive function; no endocrine or other covered organ disorder is established.
Severe neonatal encephalopathy with hypertonia and seizures; respiratory failure reflects neurologic dysfunction rather than demonstrated intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Autoantibodies directly destroy red blood cells, defining an autoimmune blood disorder.
Granulocytopenia, antibody deficiency and defining hypoglycemia; malabsorption/chronic diarrhea in 1/1. Arteritis in 1/1 omitted by cap; infections are separate episodes.
Familial cortical myoclonus is a neurologic movement disorder; falls do not establish musculoskeletal damage.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes bronchiectasis and chronic sinonasal disease in 3/3; infertility is outside the axes, and secondary infections are separate.
Cancer predisposition concerns ovarian and breast tumors, both outside the specified axes; susceptibility alone does not establish organ damage.
Clonal mast-cell proliferation is confined to skin, producing defining infiltrative lesions and blistering; systemic organ infiltration is not established.
Intellectual disability occurs in 33/33, with frequent brain malformations and seizures; facial dysmorphism does not establish additional organ dysfunction.
Infantile pulmonary disorder within the interstitial lung disease spectrum; absence of additional imaging abnormalities does not change its pulmonary location.
